root_cause.text: ext4_mb_find_by_goal() prematurely fails when ext4_mb_load_buddy() returns an error due to a corrupted group bitmap, blocking fallback to alternative groups and causing allocation failures.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check for `EXT4_MB_GRP_BBITMAP_CORRUPT(e4b->bd_info)` after the `ext4_mb_load_buddy()` error path, returning 0 (instead of the error) unless the allocation is goal-only. The commit message explains that after commit 9008a58e5dce, the corruption detection returns an error from `ext4_mb_load_buddy()`, making the subsequent corruption check in `ext4_lock_group` unreachable, so the allocation fails instead of skipping the corrupted group.

The commit message explains that after commit 9008a58e5dce, the corruption detection returns an error from `ext4_mb_load_buddy()`, making the subsequent corruption check in `ext4_lock_group` unreachable, so the allocation fails instead of skipping the corrupted group.

candidates.rationale: Normal success path that is bypassed by the early return on load_buddy error, causing allocation failure without fallback.
Call that can fail due to corrupted group bitmap, triggering the premature return and preventing fallback to alternative groups.
Condition that immediately triggers an early return when load_buddy fails, blocking any further attempts to allocate from other groups.
Direct premature return that propagates the load_buddy error, aborting the entire allocation without trying alternative groups.
Locking that is skipped when load_buddy fails, but its presence shows the intended processing that is bypassed by the early return.
Corruption check after successful load; could also cause early exit, but root cause is that even when load_buddy fails, no fallback occurs.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call may fail due to a corrupted group bitmap, setting err to a negative value. The failure triggers the early return without trying alternative groups, directly causing the vulnerability.

This condition checks the error from load_buddy and immediately jumps to the early return, not allowing fallback to alternative groups. It is the decision point that blocks further allocation attempts.
This statement directly returns the load_buddy error, aborting the entire allocation attempt. The premature return prevents the allocator from trying other groups and causes allocation failure.
This is the normal success return path. Because the error path returns early, this line is never reached when load_buddy fails, meaning the function never returns success and fallback is bypassed.

This lock is acquired only after a successful load_buddy. Its placement in the code shows the intended sequential processing that is entirely skipped when load_buddy fails, contributing to the lack of fallback.

This corruption check after successful load illustrates further processing that would occur under normal conditions. Its bypass due to the early return means that even corruption detected later would not trigger fallback, but the root cause is the premature return on load error.
